questions.question: What is LOP?
questions.answer: Unpaid leave days used to work out paid days for salary.

questions.question: What is PF?
questions.answer: Provident Fund contribution recorded in payroll, based on the applicable PF wage and rule.

questions.question: What is EPF?
questions.answer: The provident fund part of the employer contribution after the pension share.

questions.question: What is EPS?
questions.answer: The pension share of the employer contribution to provident fund.

questions.question: What is TDS?
questions.answer: Tax deducted through payroll in monthly parts toward expected yearly tax.

questions.question: What are salary arrears?
questions.answer: The difference between revised earned salary and what was actually paid for past periods.

questions.question: What is Gratuity?
questions.answer: A settlement payment that applies only when the employee meets the configured eligibility rule.

questions.question: What is leave encashment?
questions.answer: An amount for eligible unused leave, worked out under the company recorded settings.

questions.question: What is notice recovery?
questions.answer: An amount recoverable for unserved notice when recorded terms permit it and notice was not waived.

questions.question: Why did my take-home pay change?
questions.answer: Take-home pay can change due to unpaid leave, revised statutory ceilings, salary revisions, or changed tax deductions. The assistant explains recorded differences by comparing your payslips.

questions.question: Can HCM One predict my pay for next month?
questions.answer: No. The assistant explains only recorded months. It cannot promise future pay because upcoming pay depends on future attendance and inputs.

questions.question: Why is my bank deposit different from my payslip?
questions.answer: The assistant can explain only payroll records and cannot inspect your bank account. If your bank credit differs from your net pay, you can submit a query for HR.

questions.question: What does Incomplete mean?
questions.answer: A required record, input, or dependency is missing, so a full total cannot be calculated. Known line items may be shown while the full total waits for records.

questions.question: What does Cannot explain from available payroll data mean?
questions.answer: Available records do not establish the cause of a difference or dispute. When this occurs, the assistant offers to draft a query for HR.

questions.question: Can the assistant recommend which tax regime I should choose?
questions.answer: No. The assistant explains the tax recorded in your payroll under your chosen regime. It cannot recommend a tax regime or provide personal tax advice.

questions.question: Why did my monthly TDS deduction increase?
questions.answer: Monthly TDS can rise if your estimated yearly taxable income increases, such as when you declare income from a previous employer or receive a salary revision.

questions.question: How does the payroll query process work?
questions.answer: You review and confirm a draft with relevant payslip lines before it is sent. HR reviews the query, records a resolution, and you can close or dispute it.

questions.question: What do the query statuses mean?
questions.answer: Draft is unsent on your device. Sent means persisted for HR review. In review means HR is reviewing it. Resolved provides an answer, and Closed completes it.

questions.question: Can the assistant send a query to HR without my confirmation?
questions.answer: No. The assistant prepares a draft with your description and evidence, but will send it only after you explicitly confirm.

questions.question: Does approving a proposal mean payment is made?
questions.answer: No. Approving records that version and scope as ready for payroll. It does not apply the change or make a disbursement.

questions.question: Can the AI assistant approve a payroll change?
questions.answer: No. The assistant only prepares calculations and explains records. Every salary change requires human review and approval by authorized HR.

questions.question: What happens if a proposal is edited after review?
questions.answer: Editing creates a revised version. The system recalculates all affected amounts, and authorized HR must review the new version before approving.

questions.question: What does Complete for this scope mean?
questions.answer: It means required inputs and verified rules were available to calculate that specific result. It does not mean the proposal has been approved or paid.

questions.question: What does Rule not verified mean?
questions.answer: A required statutory or company rule is missing or unverified, so that calculation part is blocked. The result cannot be calculated until verified configuration is supplied.

questions.question: What does an applicable due date mean in a settlement?
questions.answer: An applicable due date is the target deadline for a specific settlement component under policy or statutory rules. It does not mean money has been paid.

questions.question: Can pending asset clearance hold my earned salary?
questions.answer: No. Clearance holds never hold earned monthly salary. Pending clearance applies only to unreturned equipment or recovery items.

questions.question: How long can exiting employees access settlement information in HCM One?
questions.answer: Settlement statements and query features remain accessible in the app while the employee has active login access. Later delivery uses company exit channels.

questions.question: Can employees see other people salary or tax details?
questions.answer: No. Strict access boundaries prevent employees from viewing any records other than their own. The assistant refuses unauthorized requests.

questions.question: Are personal identification numbers visible in the assistant?
questions.answer: No. Sensitive identifiers such as permanent account numbers and bank accounts are masked or hidden to protect privacy.

questions.question: What is HCM One and what data does it use?
questions.answer: HCM One is an agentic payroll assistant that explains calculations and prepares review drafts. It operates on fictional company data with simplified rules.
